correctness.rationale: For p∤b, the normalized digit pair is an independent digit sum. Its step vectors (1,1),(b,b^{-1}) generate precisely the index-p^min(a,v_p(b²−1)) subgroup; the integer-digit Fourier transform contracts every nontrivial character on repeated independent steps. This rigorously proves exponential convergence, normalization and every fixed-modulus probability. For p|b, two disjoint leading/trailing h=ceil(a/v_p(b)) blocks yield exact independent divisibility; a leading-digit p-adic count proves the displayed finite-length formula. Subtracting successive tails yields the valuation distribution. The actual embedded verifier passed ten exact brute-force comparisons, twelve exact group-image comparisons, and four convergence tests, which are corroborative and not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: OEIS A055483 (2000) and A161825 (2009) directly predate and tabulate the decimal and binary gcd invariants; no originality is claimed for defining them or for the base-ten 3/9 divisibility implications. Banks–Hart–Sakata 2004 studies palindromic integers, not arbitrary reversal pairs. Dartyge et al. 2023 proves binary reversible-prime and squarefree-pair counts and includes local p=3² consequences, but its checked theorem and squarefree sieve do not dominate the all-base prime-power subgroup law and exact p|b stabilization. The checked published comparisons did not reveal an equivalent full statement. Hidden implicit coverage remains a stated risk.
residual_risks: An unpublished, unindexed, or differently described proof could establish the same fixed-prime-power result.
The 2023 Fourier machinery might imply additional special cases beyond those explicitly stated, even though its principal joint-squarefree theorem does not state the present classification.
A 1969 paper on reversing digits was identified bibliographically but not read in full; its documented focus is reversal multiples, not local asymptotic gcd laws.

value.rationale: The gcd of an integer and its digit reversal is a standard enumerated arithmetic invariant (OEIS A055483). The theorem provides its complete local p-adic limiting law in every base, identifies a sharp singularity and change of geometric decay at primes dividing b²−1, proves exactly which joint residue pairs occur asymptotically, and establishes finite-length stabilization at primes dividing the base. These structural local factors are independently relevant to reversible-prime and squarefree-pair sieves (Dartyge et al. 2023), and are not a trivial normalization or a table lookup. The result claims neither a global gcd distribution nor growing-modulus uniformity.
